** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Ignore stale badge counts from superseded `updateBadge()` calls.** Overlapping `updateBadge()` calls can finish out of order. An earlier call that finishes last can overwrite a newer count, so the badge can show an outdated number until another update runs. Record a request sequence number and write the badge only when the current invocation is the latest one.
Suggested fix

```diff let badgeUpdateTimer = null; let isBadgeBusy = false; +let badgeRequestId = 0; @@ export async function updateBadge() { if (isBadgeBusy) return; + const requestId = ++badgeRequestId; try { const config = await chrome.storage.sync.get(['windowScope']); const scope = config.windowScope || 'current'; const tabs = await getMatchingTabs(scope); + if (requestId !== badgeRequestId) return; if (tabs.length > 0) { ```

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Preserve URL case when detecting an exact match.** `normalizeUrlForMatching` lowercases the pathname, query and fragment. With `example.com` active, `/Report?id=A` therefore matches an open `/report?id=a` tab. These URLs can identify different pages, but this function returns `isExactMatch: true`. Use an exact-match comparison that preserves case in these URL components. The caller must not take its duplicate-page branch for a different resource.

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Skip the name fallback for apps with explicit `domains`.** The name fallback can match an app whose explicit `domains` exclude the target URL. For example, `{name: "Calendar", domains: ["calendar.google.com"]}` matches `https://calendar.proton.me` through the `calendar` host label. `background/tab-mover.js` then sends that app's `id` as `appId` in the `LAUNCH` payload, so the URL can open in an unrelated application. Apply the name fallback only to apps that do not supply `domains`. The fallback still covers apps with missing metadata, which the discovery code handles.
Suggested fix

```diff --- "a/utils/window-matcher.js" +++ "b/utils/window-matcher.js" @@ -166,14 +166,15 @@ // Name fallback only after every app failed the domain checks, and only as a // whole host label: "Mail" must not match gmail.com. const hostLabels = targetHostname.split('.').map((l) => l.replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, '')); for (const app of candidates) { if (app.name && typeof app.name === 'string') { const cleanName = app.name.toLowerCase().replace(/[^a-z0-9]/g, ''); - if (cleanName.length >= 4 && hostLabels.includes(cleanName)) { + const hasExplicitDomains = Array.isArray(app.domains) && app.domains.length > 0; + if (!hasExplicitDomains && cleanName.length >= 4 && hostLabels.includes(cleanName)) { return app; } } } return null; } ```
Committable suggestion

> **IMPORTANT** > Review the replacement and indentation, then test before committing. ```suggestion const hasExplicitDomains = Array.isArray(app.domains) && app.domains.length > 0; if (!hasExplicitDomains && cleanName.length >= 4 && hostLabels.includes(cleanName)) { ```

** Minor** · **Functional Correctness** · **Quick win** **Group installed apps that provide `appLaunchUrl` without `domains`.** The management fallback produces this record shape. `findMatchingInstalledApp` accepts it through launch-host matching, but this predicate always rejects it. For an app launched at `https://example.com`, tabs at `a.example.com` and `b.example.com` become separate hostname groups when no preset or active domain applies. Launch matching identifies both as the same installed app. Apply compatible installed-app matching here so grouping uses the app's ID and name.
